naslov: NBA betting: One bet to make on every team heading into the season
tekst:
The 2025-26 NBA season tips off Tuesday, and the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are co-favorites to win the NBA championship (+270). Right behind them are the defending champion New York Knicks and upgraded Philadelphia 76ers, both at +900.
While not every team is a contender, every team still offers a chance to make a bet. We tasked NBA betting experts Andre Snellings and Eric Moody to sort through the possibilities and suggest a future bet on every team this season.
Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.
Snellings on the Eastern Conference
Atlanta Hawks
Bet: To make playoffs (-145), to win Southeast Division (+320)
The Hawks traded Trae Young on Jan. 7, and after that trade finished with a 29-15 regular-season record that was the seventh best in the NBA in that span. The Hawks then went up two games to one on the eventual champion New York Knicks in the playoffs, the only team to win two games against the Knicks this past postseason. The Hawks return their core that finished the season, led by budding star Jalen Johnson, and supplemented that with two contributors from the Oklahoma City Thunder championship team (Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins) as well as a lottery pick in Kingston Flemings. They seem poised to continue to improve upon their strong finish.
Boston Celtics
Bet: OVER 51.5 wins (-105)
The Celtics are in a new regime after the Jaylen Brown trade, but in many ways this team is analogous to the one last season when Jayson Tatum was out. In both situations, they built a team around one of the two stars who have led them for the past near-decade. Last season, Brown led the Celtics to 56 wins. This season's team has better balance than last, with Mitchell Robinson brought in at center and Paul George, when healthy, as new additions to the rest of the core. Last season's 56 wins are a reasonable goal for this team, making over 51.5 wins solid value.
Brooklyn Nets
Bet: Mikel Brown Jr. to be named first-team All-Rookie (+220)
Brown was the fifth pick in the NBA draft and projects to be the starting guard for the Nets from Day 1. He is a polished perimeter offense creator and has the potential to be among the leaders in both points and assists in this class. While this is a deep draft class with a lot of talent, Brown has a better than 2-to-1 chance to play his way onto the first team.
Charlotte Hornets
Bet: To participate in play-in tournament (+130)
The Hornets were the ninth seed in the Eastern Conference last season, one of four play-in teams. They finished 12 games ahead of the 11th-seeded Bucks, who have since traded away franchise MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Hornets are an up-and-coming team, led by two perimeter scoring wings in Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel, and they also have a strengthened front line after bringing in Naz Reid in exchange for point guard LaMelo Ball this offseason. The lack of Ball may limit their upside enough to keep them out of the playoffs, but they should still be significantly better than the non-play-in caliber teams.
Chicago Bulls
Bet: Caleb Wilson to win Rookie of the Year (+350)
Wilson was one of the four candidates to be drafted No. 1 overall in this year's historic NBA draft, and that was on the strength of his elite athleticism, defensive upside and slasher/finisher offensive game he displayed in college. But in the Las Vegas Summer League, Wilson displayed a brand new proclivity for taking and making 3-pointers off both the catch-and-shoot and off the dribble. If Wilson continues to display that shooting in the NBA, he has serious Rookie of the Year upside, particularly as he settles in as the face and franchise player for a fast-paced Bulls unit, which could lead to big numbers.
Cleveland Cavaliers
Bet: To qualify for conference semifinals (+125), win Central Division (+195)
The Cavaliers were the top seed in the Eastern Conference two seasons ago after winning 64 games with a +9.5 PPG scoring margin. Last season, after a down regular season inspired in part by injuries to point guard Darius Garland, the Cavaliers rode the late-season trade of Garland for James Harden and played their way to the Eastern Conference finals. While the Eastern Conference as a whole got stronger this offseason, the Cavaliers should return a team with the same key players who have demonstrated the capacity for success in both the regular season and playoffs. To be able to bet them, at plus money, to make it a round earlier than they made it last season is value, even in the new Eastern Conference.
Detroit Pistons
Bet: Cade Cunningham to be named first-team All-NBA (+275)
Cunningham has been All-NBA in each of the last two seasons, was third team in 2024-25 and first team last season. He finished top seven in the MVP voting in both seasons, and at age 25 he is still improving. Cunningham led a young Pistons team to the top seed in the Eastern Conference last season, and if he plays at a similar level this season he has a much better than 2.75-to-1 chance to repeat his slot on the First Team.
Indiana Pacers
Bet: Tyrese Haliburton regular-season assists-per-game leader (+450)
Haliburton is returning after missing all last season with a torn Achilles. In his three full seasons with the Pacers before his injury, Haliburton averaged 10.2 APG. He led the NBA in the 2023-24 season with 10.9 APG. The Pacers run their entire offense through Haliburton; they ranked top 10 in the NBA in team offensive rating in his last two seasons with them (second in 2023-24) but fell to 29th last season without him. With Haliburton back at the helm, the offense should return to high efficiency and Haliburton should again rack up assists.
